Ever since I was young, I have always been triggered by two things. Unfairness and illogical situations. The odd thing here is that life never treated me unfairly, or at least not as unfairly as it treats some other people. I am white. I was born in a safe, loving family. My dad has always had a good job, which meant I never had to think twice about buying clothes, going on a holiday, or even studying. I lived in a great house with all comfort you can wish for as a kid. Yes, I was born privileged.

Despite not having experienced fundamental unfairness myself, the urge to fight against unfairness has always been deep-rooted in my character. I was 11 years old when this led to concrete action for the first time.

When I was 11 years old I went to high school, together with my twin sister Fleur. When we arrived for our very first day, we immediately got to know Richard, the school janitor. Richard was a black, 50-year-old man whose working life had never been easy and fair. Yet, he was without a doubt the most grateful, enthusiastic, and motivated employee of the entire school. Every morning when we arrived at school, Richard was there to help us find a spot for our bikes. To help us fix our broken lockers. Or just to listen to students when none of the teachers did.

After six months of going to high school, the school principal sent an email to all students, stating that Richard would be leaving the school within the next month. His job had become ‘redundant’ - something that I never believed The same day, me, Fleur, and some friends decided to organise a strike. No one would be going to their class if Richard couldn’t stay. So, the day after the principal announced Richard’s leave, the entire school, counting 1.100 students, went on strike. We called every newspaper and news channel we knew, after which the story made it not only to the local newspaper but even to national TV channels. This left the school with no other choice than to withdraw Richard’s termination.

10 years later, I decided to translate my two personal triggers into a business. Together with Fleur, I started Equalture, a fast-growing HR tech scaleup based in The Netherlands. We are on a mission to shape the world of unbiased hiring, by merging the art of neuroscience and gamification.

My first years of being an entrepreneur have led me to several nominations, including Forbes 30 Under 30, Harper's Bazaar Women of the Year 2022, Top 30 Most Inclusive Leaders NL, LOEY Talent Award, Sprout 25 under 25 and Sifted's top 14 European Gen Z Founders.
